title: Choose the Visioning deck path
objective: Select the approach for a customer with ten candidate workflows and for one with none.
clearance: Rewritten draft; pending SME and partner clearance

blocks.x: Visioning should start where the customer is. Some customers arrive with a list of AI ideas. Others have no list at all. Each needs a different path through the session.

items: **The customer has a use case list.** Validate and prioritize it. Spend most of the session completing the use case fields: persona, workflow, pain, data sources, impact and effort rationale, and uncertainties. Then negotiate placement on the impact/effort 2x2.

**The customer has no list.** Bring an informed hypothesis and relevant departmental examples, then draw out real workflows tied to outcomes. Glean's Blueprint material provides sample department 2x2s for this. Sometimes you will need a mini Visioning session with each department to understand its priorities.

blocks.x: "What could AI do for you?" invites vague wishes. Use departmental thought starters and focused questions about recurring work instead. Ask what takes time, what goes wrong, and what the consequence is.
Example use cases help customers recognize their own work. They do not prove that a use case is feasible or valuable for this customer. Don't replace listening with a tour of a use case catalog.

blocks.label: Tip
blocks.x: If you show examples, present a few that are relevant to the department in the room and say plainly that they are there to be changed, merged, or discarded.
The customer's starting point decides the deck path. Either way, you end with ranked use cases and owners.

blocks.title: Two Visioning starting points
blocks.alt: A comparison of the two Visioning paths. When the customer has a use case list, validate and rank it against outcomes. When the customer has no list, start from priorities and pain, use relevant examples as prompts, and build the list together.
